newsitem.title: USA: Simpson case expert backs down on two-killer theory.
newsitem.headline: Simpson case expert backs down on two-killer theory.

text.p: A forensic expert who earlier testified that two asssailants may have murdered O.J. Simpson's ex-wife and her friend conceded on Tuesday that the facts pointed to only one killer.

Michael Baden, New York State Police medical examiner, also said under cross-examination in Simpson's civil wrongful death trial that the fatal wounds suffered by Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman were consistent with one knife.

Baden, who was called by Simpson's defence in the civil case and who also testified on the ex-football star's behalf in his criminal trial, backed down on his previous insistence that Goldman struggled with his killer for five to 10 minutes before finally succumbing to his wounds.

He had told the jurors on Monday that Goldman was probably on his feet for five to 10 minutes after he was stabbed in the neck, as evidenced by a flow of blood running down his shirt and pants and into his shoe.

But Edward Medvene, a plaintiffs lawyer, showed him crime scene photographs on Tuesday indicating there was no flow of blood from Goldman's shirt onto his pants and argued that the blood on the pants came from a stab wound to the thigh.
Baden then said Goldman may have stayed alive for only "two to three minutes" after receiving his fatal neck wound.
The length of the struggle is important because lawyers for the plaintiffs contend the murders were committed outside Nicole Simpson's condominium at about 10:35 to 10:40 p.m.
O.J. Simpson was spotted in his driveway by a limousine driver at about 10:55 p.m. The less time it took to commit the murders, the more time he had to get back to his mansion two miles (3 km) away.
Simpson was acquitted in October 1995 of criminal charges in the June 12, 1994, murders. He is fighting a wrongful death lawsuit by the victims families, who seek damages.

Baden testified on Monday on direct examination he reached the conclusion that more than one assailant was involved because "it would have been very difficult for a single perpetrator to control multiple victims in a public place."
"I can't understand how these two people were murdered and not yell out unless there were two people there," he said.

But asked on Tuesday by Medvene, "Would it be fair to say that based on the facts you know of, that the facts are consistent with only one assailant?" Baden replied, "It would be consistent with one person."
Medvene then asked, "It would be your testimony that all of the knife wounds are consistent with being delivered by one knife?"
"Yes, could be," Baden responded. He also agreed that with the kind of fatal injuries sustained by the victims the assailant need not have been injured in the attack.
But Baden said the chance that curved abrasions on the back of Simpson's left hand were caused by one or both of the victims' fingernails were, "One tenth of one percent."

He also noted Simpson's skin was not found underneath the fingernails of Nicole Brown Simpson or Goldman, but he agreed with Medvene that it was "very rare" to find skin under fingernails in such cases.
